note: Hard-coded Korean string literals left per client (area of scripts/check-locales.js). The count must equal its area's budget: more is a new literal, fewer means the budget is stale; lower it with node scripts/check-locales.js --write-budget, which never raises one. Stage 2-1 added a last-resort count of Hangul the literal pattern cannot see (inside interpolations and Swift/C# """ blocks), so the other areas were re-based on that true count: macOS core 872→874, WinUI 189→190, phone 202→219; Windows Core fell 161→137 when SlashCommandStrings moved to the shared keys macOS reads. Exemptions and allowed literals are not counted; each says why, and one that no longer matches anything fails the check. Stage 2-2 moved macOS core to the shared keys (874→0): the frozen style engine (Styles/**, v6) and the Hangul composer's jamo tables are exempt, and saved-data markers, the status-line trust names and reply matchers are allowed. Stage 2-3 moved Windows Core (137→0) and WinUI (190→0) to the shared keys: the WinUI GUI smoke (MainWindow.Smoke.cs) is exempt and the status-line trust names stay as written; --touched-since now leaves out what the budget exempts or allows. Hangul spelled as \uXXXX / \u{XXXX} escapes is decoded before counting, so escapes cannot hide a literal: the Windows matchers and smoke fixtures written that way are allowed or exempt by name.
